tips: Load your Suica/Pasmo into your Apple/Google Wallet while you still have free airport Wi-Fi at MSP.
Set your phone timezone to JST (UTC+9) right after takeoff to start syncing your sleep cycle to Tokyo time.
Hit the Limousine Bus ticket counter at Haneda before grabbing your bags to secure spots for all 8.
Use the Tokyo Metropolitan Gov't Building free observatory if you want a skyline view without spending yen on night one.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are dry but cold (often near 40°F/5°C). The Shibuya Blue Cave outdoor illumination walk will feel biting, especially after sunset.
tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if unbooked, pivot immediately to Mag's Park rooftop or Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby.
Layer up for the Blue Cave walk—it's all outdoors along the wind-tunneled Shibuya River.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: High rain risk in mid-December. Senso-ji and Nakamise are partially outdoors, and Ueno Ameyoko is an open-air market.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h) slots between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line.
suggestedSwap.reason: Heavy rain makes the open-air Ameyoko market miserable; the Tokyo National Museum is a world-class indoor alternative right in Ueno Park.

tips: If it rains, buy a clear konbini umbrella (¥500) for the Nakamise stretch, then head indoors.
Skytree queues can be brutal in bad weather as outdoor tourists pivot indoors; check the Asahi Beer Hall Sky Room alternative.
teamLab Planets requires walking barefoot in water; roll your pants up and wear easily removable shoes.
Golden Gai bars seat 4-6 max; split into two squads of 4 and use WhatsApp to share good spots.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: Coastal Kamakura and Enoshima are highly exposed to winter winds and rain. The Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset requires clear skies.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining or excessively windy, the exposed Sea Candle climb will be miserable; Enospa provides a warm, scenic indoor alternative.

tips: Check the morning weather forecast; if it's totally overcast, swap the Enoshima coastal tram segment for Hokokuji's indoor bamboo grove and matcha.
The Enoden local train is charming but slow; if you're running late, the Shonan Shinjuku line is faster to Fujisawa.
Run the Airbnb laundry during dinner so everyone packs clean clothes for the Kyoto leg.
Thermae-Yu requires tattoos to be covered; bring waterproof bandages if anyone in the group has ink.
Sit on the LEFT side of the Nozomi shinkansen (Seat E) for the best chance at a Mt. Fuji view around minute 40.
Pontocho Alley restaurants are tiny; confirm your reservation for 8 is locked in, as walk-ins for large groups are nearly impossible.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn is entirely outdoors and exposed to cold December winds on the mountain.
tips: Wear layers and heat-tech for the Fushimi Inari dawn hike; it's significantly colder at the Yotsutsuji intersection.
Funaoka Onsen has a famous 'electric bath'—start on the low setting before you fully commit.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove offers little shelter in rain, and Iwatayama Monkey Park is dangerously slippery on wet steps. Nara deer park is entirely exposed.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Iwatayama Monkey Park — humans enter the cage
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kimono Forest at Randen Arashiyama station: pillar-lit fabric columns glowing at dusk — free, on the way out anyway.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the steep 20-30 min hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park becomes a slippery, cold mud pit; the Kimono Forest is covered and easily accessible.

tips: Nara deer can be aggressive with food; buy deer crackers one pack at a time and show empty hands when done.
Wakakusa-yama is closed for the year as of Dec 13—don't accidentally start the climb!
KFC for Christmas Eve is no joke in Japan—pre-order your bucket days in advance online or expect a 2-hour line.
Nintendo Museum lottery tickets are strict; have your QR codes and IDs ready for entry.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at maximum capacity. Super Nintendo World timed entry will be fiercely contested.
tips: Rope-drop 45 minutes early and sprint directly to Super Nintendo World the second the gates open.
If Express Passes are sold out, rely on single-rider lines for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey to save 60% of the wait.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima island is highly exposed to sea winds. The floating torii gate viewing and Omotesando street are outdoor-heavy.
tips: The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally heavy; it's okay to step out to the park if someone needs a breather.
Check the tide schedule—high tide is required to see the torii 'floating', while low tide lets you walk out to it.
Midosuji Illumination is best photographed after sunset; start the Umeda Sky Building at 16:30 to catch the transition.
Misono Building bars are tiny; split into groups of 2-4 to actually find seats in the micro-bars.

2026-12-28.weatherAlert: Himeji Castle involves extensive outdoor walking and steep, cold stone staircases in December.
tips: Wear thick socks and easy-slip shoes for Himeji Castle; you must remove shoes inside the main keep and the floors are freezing.
Do your final tax-free shopping tonight in Namba; verify all receipts are stapled in your passports for airport customs.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat A/E) of the Nozomi for one last Mt. Fuji view on the ride back to Tokyo.
Zero-out your Suica cards by buying snacks or using the station top-up machines; you can't get a refund on the balance.

globalTips: The USD/JPY rate is highly favorable at ~161.85. Use a card with no foreign transaction fees for large purchases, but carry cash (withdrawn from 7-Eleven ATMs) for smaller shops, temples, and konbini runs.
With 8 people, always split into 2-4 person squads for restaurants, bars, and arcade lanes—Japan's venues rarely seat large groups together.
December in Japan is cold and dry but occasionally rainy. Pack Uniqlo Heat-Tech, a windproof outer layer, and a compact umbrella; clear konbini umbrellas (¥500) are great backups for sudden showers.
